transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time with this, because it feels a little embarrassing to even talk about, honestly. 

But, well, I guess what brings me in is that I keep getting sort of... stuck on how my face looks lately. Specifically, there's this sagging, kind of uneven look around my jaw and on one side of my face. It really started bothering me after I saw myself in a bunch of recent family photos, and now I just can't seem to unsee it. 

My wife, and even a few of my clients at the firm, they all tell me they barely notice anything at all, which is really nice of them to say, but I just can't seem to shake it. Does that... does that make sense to you? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it okay and that I'm in the right place.
How much has this concern about your face affected your daily life or the way you interact with others?

Well, I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I'm falling apart or anything, because I'm definitely not. I still get through my work just fine, and I make sure my clients are taken care of. I wouldn't let this get in the way of my responsibilities, you know? 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it has been a little distracting. I've found myself taking a bit longer to get out the door for client meetings, just... checking the mirror one more time, trying to make sure the lighting isn't catching my jaw the wrong way. And maybe I've been a little less, um, present during a few of those appointments because it's sort of running in the back of my mind. 

I did actually skip a couple of local art openings recently with my wife, too. I just... I knew people would be taking pictures, and I really didn't want to be seen or photographed looking like this. I know that sounds a bit silly for a grown man to say, and I hope you don't think less of me for it. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you find yourself thinking about this facial concern for hours each day, or does it feel difficult to control or push aside these thoughts, even when you try?

Oh, no, definitely not hours. I... I really wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting around obsessing over it all day, because I'm definitely not. I mean, I have my practice to run, and I need to be sharp for my clients, right? 

So I can definitely push it aside when I need to focus. It's not... it's not completely out of my control or anything like that. I guess I've never really timed it, but it's probably just a few moments here and there when I happen to pass a mirror, or maybe just a passing thought. It's really not taking over my whole day. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture and not, you know, exaggerating things. Am I answering your questions okay so far?

When you notice your facial concern, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking mirrors, adjusting your face, or trying to cover it up—or thinking about it in a certain way to try to feel better?

Well, um... I guess I do a few little things, but nothing too extreme, I promise. Like, before a client meeting, I might just pop into the bathroom real quick to check the mirror, and maybe just glance at my phone camera a couple of times. Just to, you know, make sure the lighting isn't making that side of my face look worse than it is. 

Sometimes I'll adjust my collar a bit, or just try to figure out the best angle to hold my head so it's less noticeable. It's just about putting my best foot forward for the clients, really. 

And, um, I have noticed that when I'm at an art gallery event with my wife, or even just looking at some of the younger advisors at the firm... I might catch myself sort of comparing my jawline to theirs. Just for a second. And then I realize I haven't been paying full attention to what they're saying. 

But it's just a habit I've picked up recently, and I'm sure I can get a handle on it. I hope that doesn't sound too strange or vain? I just want to be completely honest with you so you can do your job. Does that sound fairly normal to you?
Have these concerns about your facial appearance caused you significant distress, or made you avoid certain situations like the art openings you mentioned?

Well, um... like I touched on a little bit ago, I really wouldn't use a heavy phrase like 'significant distress.' I definitely don't want you to think I'm falling to pieces over this, because I promise I'm not. I still get through my work just fine, and I always make sure my clients are taken care of. 

But... yeah, I guess it has affected things a little bit. Like I mentioned earlier, I’ve been a bit slower getting out the door for client meetings, and maybe less present during some of those appointments than I normally would be. And... yes, I did avoid those few art openings. I just really didn't want to be seen or photographed by anyone looking the way I do right now. 

I know it sounds a bit ridiculous for a guy my age to avoid a nice evening out over something like that... I really hope you don't judge me too harshly for it. I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions exactly the way you need me to. Does that give you the information you're looking for?
